book.title_zh: 凯莱 (Cayley) 图和相关的问题

questions.formal_statement: Does every finite flag-transitive projective plane have to be Desarguesian? Equivalently, for n>8 with p=n^2+n+1 prime, show D={x in F_p*: x^(n+1)=1} is not a planar difference set.
questions.relation_to_book: The geometric nonexistence conjecture is explicitly stated in the article. Its literal diameter-two Cayley-graph assertion is inconsistent; disclose it rather than silently correcting it.
questions.solved_means: A proof for every order n>8 that no non-Desarguesian finite flag-transitive projective plane exists (equivalently, no special prime p=n^2+n+1), or an explicit counterexample plane verified directly.

identified_counterpart.zh_quote: 直径为 3 的图 Cay(p) 的存在性等价于 n 阶非 -Desarguesian 旗传递射影平面的存在性, 参见文献 [2]∼[4]. 后者是几何学中的一个重要问题, 其不存在性是几何学中一个著名的猜想.
identified_counterpart.en: …the existence of a graph Cay(p) of diameter 3 is equivalent to the existence of a non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective plane of order n; see [2]–[4]. The latter is an important problem in geometry, and its non-existence is a famous conjecture in geometry.
names: Flag-transitive projective plane conjecture: every finite flag-transitive projective plane is Desarguesian
Non-existence of non-Desarguesian flag-transitive finite projective planes
Frobenius (sharply flag-transitive) case of Kantor's theorem on flag-transitive projective planes
Feit's question about primes p = n^2+n+1: is the subgroup of (n+1)-th roots of unity mod p a planar difference set?
Planar difference sets that are multiplicative subgroups of F_p^* (cyclotomic planar difference sets)
非 Desarguesian 旗传递射影平面的不存在性猜想
有限旗传递射影平面都是 Desarguesian 平面的猜想
identified_counterpart.formal_statement: Setting printed in the article: n > 8 is an integer such that p = n² + n + 1 is prime. [ASSUMPTION: standard definitions supplied] A projective plane of order n has n²+n+1 points and n²+n+1 lines. Each line is incident with n+1 points and each point with n+1 lines. Any two distinct points lie on exactly one common line, and any two distinct lines meet in exactly one point. The plane is Desarguesian if it is isomorphic to PG(2,q) over a finite field F_q (then n = q). It is flag-transitive if some group of collineations is transitive on its flags (incident point–line pairs). Conjecture (the article says 'its non-existence is a famous conjecture in geometry'): for no such n does a non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective plane of order n exist. Citing [2]–[4], the article links this to the non-existence of a diameter-3 graph Cay(p); as printed, that Cayley-graph wording is defective (see q4). [ASSUMPTION — supplied general form, using Kantor [3] as cited: a non-Desarguesian flag-transitive plane of order n forces p = n²+n+1 to be prime and a Frobenius group of order p(n+1) to act sharply flag-transitively. Every projective plane of order ≤ 8 is Desarguesian, so the printed conjecture is equivalent to 'every finite flag-transitive projective plane is Desarguesian'.] [ASSUMPTION — supplied number-theoretic form, NOT printed in the article: equivalently, for every n > 8 with p = n²+n+1 prime, the subgroup D = {x ∈ F_p^* : x^{n+1} = 1} (|D| = n+1) is not a planar (p, n+1, 1) difference set in (Z_p, +). That is, the n(n+1) = p − 1 differences d − d′ (d ≠ d′ in D) do not cover all nonzero residues mod p. For n = 2 and n = 8 this D is a planar difference set, giving PG(2,2) and PG(2,8); this fits the article's restriction n > 8.]
identified_counterpart.solved_means: Either a proof that for every n > 8 with p = n²+n+1 prime there is no non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective plane of order n, or a counterexample. By the supplied reformulations, a proof is the same as showing that every finite flag-transitive projective plane is Desarguesian, or that μ_{n+1} ⊂ F_p^* is never a planar difference set mod p for such n. A counterexample would be an explicit non-Desarguesian flag-transitive plane, e.g. an n > 8 with p = n²+n+1 prime for which μ_{n+1} is a planar difference set mod p. Ruling out ranges or congruence classes of n is only partial progress.

verdicts.source: Binzhou Xia, [New necessary conditions for the existence of finite non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective planes](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.05486), European Journal of Combinatorics 110 (2023), 103687, DOI 10.1016/j.ejc.2023.103687; full text checked in author manuscript v7.

Cai Heng Li, [Finite s-arc transitive Cayley graphs and flag-transitive projective planes](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228757029_Finite_s-arc_transitive_Cayley_graphs_and_flag-transitive_projective_planes), Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 133 (2005), 31–41, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9939-04-07549-5.

literature.summary: As of 2026-10-15, q3 remains open in the checked literature: [Thas–Zagier (2008)](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.4171/JEMS/107/fulltext.pdf) exclude n<200000000000, while Xia's 2023 paper supplies further necessary conditions. Literal q4 is false by bipartiteness, with classical diameter-three counterexamples also furnished by [Li (2005), Example 4.5](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228757029_Finite_s-arc_transitive_Cayley_graphs_and_flag-transitive_projective_planes).

sources.citation: Koen Thas and Don Zagier, [Finite projective planes, Fermat curves, and Gaussian periods](https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.4171/JEMS/107/fulltext.pdf), Journal of the European Mathematical Society 10 (2008), 173–190, DOI 10.4171/JEMS/107.
sources.finding: Sections 1–3, using Kantor, justify q3's special-prime reformulation with D=(F_p^×)^n=μ_(n+1). The appendix, p.189, reports exclusion for n<200000000000 using necessary congruences and modular exponentiation. This is a finite computational result, not an all-orders proof; no larger plane-order exclusion was located in the checked literature.

sources.citation: Binzhou Xia, [New necessary conditions for the existence of finite non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective planes](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.05486), European Journal of Combinatorics 110 (2023), 103687, DOI 10.1016/j.ejc.2023.103687; full text checked in author manuscript v7.
sources.finding: Conjecture 1.1 is exactly q3. Theorem 1.3 gives necessary polynomial-system conditions over finite fields of characteristic 3, including extension fields rather than just F_3. Section 5 conjectures their general inconsistency rather than proving it. Theorem 3.7 excludes 26th- and 32nd-cyclotomic difference sets in prime fields; these index results do not extend the published plane-order range.

sources.citation: William M. Kantor, [Primitive permutation groups of odd degree, and an application to finite projective planes](https://pages.uoregon.edu/kantor/PAPERS/odddegree_planes.pdf), Journal of Algebra 106 (1987), 15–45.
sources.finding: Theorem A leaves, besides the classical alternative, a Frobenius group of odd order (n²+n+1)(n+1), with n²+n+1 prime. This supplies the group-theoretic reduction and forces n even, but does not eliminate that alternative. Its proof uses the classification of finite simple groups.

sources.citation: Walter Feit, [Finite projective planes and a question about primes](https://paperzz.com/doc/9103748/finite-projective-planes-and-a-question-about-primes), Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 108 (1990), 561–564; primary article read through a full-text transcription.
sources.finding: Lemma 2.1 supplies d^(n+1)≡1 mod p for every positive divisor d of a putative nonclassical plane order n; Lemma 2.2 supplies 8|n. Taking d=n and using ord_p(n)=3 gives n≡2 mod 3. The additional power-of-two exclusion in Theorem A has a defective argument, identified by later literature, and is not imported here.

sources.citation: Cai Heng Li, [Finite s-arc transitive Cayley graphs and flag-transitive projective planes](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/228757029_Finite_s-arc_transitive_Cayley_graphs_and_flag-transitive_projective_planes), Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 133 (2005), 31–41, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9939-04-07549-5.
sources.finding: Example 4.5 supplies Cayley realizations of classical projective-plane incidence graphs using Singer groups and a duality. At n=17, p=307, this gives an admissible reflection-generated dihedral Cayley graph of degree 18 and diameter 3: a counterexample to literal q4. The paper's separate Γ(q) construction specifies an automorphism orbit; it does not justify the book's arbitrary-S equivalence or diameter-two assertion. The valid q3 reduction used here comes from Kantor plus Thas–Zagier.

sources.citation: Binzhou Xia, [Cyclotomic difference sets in finite fields](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.03275), Mathematics of Computation 87 (2018), 2461–2482, DOI 10.1090/mcom/3311.
sources.finding: Develops character-sum and polynomial criteria for cyclotomic and modified cyclotomic difference sets, including nonexistence for even indices through 22 other than 2,4,8. Section 5.3 explicitly connects planar difference sets to q3 and retains the conjecture. Its characteristic-two classification does not settle q3, whose ambient field F_p has odd prime order.

sources.citation: Koji Momihara, Qi Wang and Qing Xiang, [Cyclotomy, difference sets, sequences with low correlation, strongly regular graphs, and related geometric substructures](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.03007), in Combinatorics and Finite Fields (2019), 173–198.
sources.finding: The survey's Section 2.1 and Theorem 2.6 connect q3 to the broader cyclotomic difference-set classification conjectures. It retains these conjectures and discusses the computational exclusion. It also warns that Feit's power-of-two exclusion and Ott's prime-power-order argument contain errors; their combination is not an accepted solution.

sources.citation: Pingzhi Yuan and Hu Yahui, [A note on power residue difference sets](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/256735294_A_note_on_power_residue_difference_sets), Journal of Algebra 291 (2005), 269–273, DOI 10.1016/j.jalgebra.2004.09.029.
sources.finding: Identifies a gap invalidating the proofs of Ott's principal power-residue and sharply flag-transitive-plane conclusions. This is primary evidence against treating the older apparent resolution as established; it does not itself resolve q3.

angles.angle: Validate the imported reduction and reproduce controls before production.
angles.deliverable: A premise ledger naming Kantor's classification-dependent reduction, the Thas–Zagier special-prime and base-two criteria, Feit's valid 8|n and divisor-multiplier conditions, and the derivation ord_p(n)=3 ⇒ 3|(n+1). Reproduce the published base-two exceptional list 2,8,24,90,512,134217728,297474474 with explicit control-interval coverage; isolated positive checks must not be represented as reproducing the full list. Include proper-divisor guards so primes in the controls are not sieved by themselves.

angles.angle: Attempt a finite range extension using a segmented divisor sieve followed by exact base-two modular tests.
angles.deliverable: After controls pass, start at n=200000000000 inclusive, restrict to n≡8 mod24, and aim for n<2000000000000. The target contains 75000000000 candidates before sieving, so benchmark first and cap production at about 2.5 hours. Reject by a sieve factor only when 1<q<p. Use correct full-width intermediate products for the proposed 128-bit Montgomery implementation. For every block, require sieved count plus tested count to equal its exact arithmetic-class count; report N only at the last unbroken audited block boundary.

angles.angle: Resolve every surviving candidate with an exact witness.
angles.deliverable: A survivor/elimination table recording n, p and a checkable reason: an explicit proper factor of p, or failure of a proved necessary condition such as d^(n+1)≡1 mod p for a divisor d of n. A probable-prime result never eliminates a survivor. Candidates without exact elimination remain explicitly unresolved and prevent exclusion claims covering them.

angles.angle: Audit arithmetic and coverage with a separate arbitrary-precision implementation.
angles.deliverable: At production-sized moduli, compare complete 2^(n+1) mod p residues and actual sieve divisors. Recompute contiguous audit windows with arbitrary precision and hash every (n, decision, full residue) record in those windows; include boundary cases and known positive controls. Preserve production logs and use python3 or preinstalled tools for replay checks, without executing attack-built binaries. State exactly which subsets received independent checking; neither sampling nor hashes independently certify the entire production scan.

acceptance.solved: A proof for every order n>8 that no non-Desarguesian finite flag-transitive projective plane exists (equivalently, no special prime p=n^2+n+1), or an explicit counterexample plane verified directly.
acceptance.refuted: a verified counterexample or negative answer to the stated question itself
acceptance.partial: An exactly scoped verified result, such as a gap-free finite range 200000000000<=n<N with every survivor eliminated under declared imported premises, or a proved new necessary condition.

owner_selection.title_zh: 凯莱 (Cayley) 图和相关的问题
owner_selection.question: Does every finite flag-transitive projective plane have to be Desarguesian? Equivalently, for n>8 with p=n^2+n+1 prime, show D={x in F_p*: x^(n+1)=1} is not a planar difference set.
owner_selection.relation_to_book: The geometric nonexistence conjecture is explicitly stated in the article. Its literal diameter-two Cayley-graph assertion is inconsistent; disclose it rather than silently correcting it.
owner_selection.baseline: Thas-Zagier, JEMS10(2008): no non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective plane for order n<200000000000. No later range extension located in the dated screen.
owner_selection.bounded_target: Try to extend the computed nonexistence range to at least n<2000000000000, with exact interval coverage, known-case controls, a survivor/elimination table, and independent checks. Any finite range is a sub-question only.
owner_selection.angle: Harden the staged segmented prime-divisor sieve plus 128-bit Montgomery base-two test on n=8 mod24. Restrict sieve rejection to proper divisors q<p. Controls must reproduce the published exceptional list. Declare the imported Feit/congruence theorems.
owner_selection.risk: High plausibility for a producing range extension is inference, not a promise of proof. Sampled Python pow cross-checks and hashes do not certify every tested n; report that limit explicitly. Do not attack the trivial false literal diameter claim. Probable-prime survivors remain unresolved, not eliminated.
review_requirements: Do not say the target is the book Cayley-graph form or follows from the book stated equivalence. Disclose both printed problems: reflection-generated dihedral Cayley graphs are bipartite with degree smaller than either part, so diameter two is impossible; and the unspecified reflection set breaks the printed equivalence (classical Singer difference sets give diameter-three graphs for Desarguesian planes). Credit the reduction to Kantor plus Thas-Zagier.

Declare every imported premise: Kantor 1987 (relies on the classification of finite simple groups), the Thas-Zagier special-prime reduction and base-two condition, Feit 8|n, and the derivation of n congruent to 2 modulo 3.
Before the main scan, add the proper-divisor guard q

Cross-checks at main-range modulus sizes must compare full 2^(n+1) mod p residues and actual sieve divisors, not only survivor flags. Any contiguous hash must include every n decision and residue. A uniform failing big-integer bug must not masquerade as no survivors.

A probable-prime test cannot eliminate a survivor. Each survivor needs an exact elimination reason, such as an explicit proper factor or a proved necessary-condition failure; otherwise list it as unresolved.
Cap the main production scan at about 2.5 hours. Report N only as the end of the last unbroken audited block.

Defensible success wording: Assuming the declared imported theorems, one production computation excluded all candidates for 200000000000<=n<N in the audited congruence class; independent arbitrary-precision checks covered only stated subsets. Therefore no non-Desarguesian flag-transitive plane of order less than N exists, conditional on those premises. Never say the extended range was independently certified, and keep the all-orders conjecture open.

Previous attack-e0 is copied automatically. Recovered compressed production logs are under selection-inputs/first-attempt-logs/ and must be reconstructed and hash-checked against its manifest without importing producer code. The previous referee result is unverified: logs were absent; sieved-plus-tested counts are not decision audits; Python/C comparison must cross-check arithmetic, not only aggregate counts. Every replay command must finish under 900 seconds.

Continuation: the parent sandbox replay passed all epoch-1 claim commands, including chunks 06-09 and all window groups, but the referee replay ran out of time. Main open verification gap: the extended range rests on one C production run. Best bounded next step: an independently implemented exhaustive recomputation with different multiword arithmetic, first for [200000000000,2000000000000), comparing every decision and full residue or a per-block hash of them; then extend if time remains. Consolidate commands so all replay fits.
owner_selection.solved_means: A proof for every order n>8 that no non-Desarguesian finite flag-transitive projective plane exists (equivalently, no special prime p=n^2+n+1), or an explicit counterexample plane verified directly.
owner_selection.partial_means: An exactly scoped verified result, such as a gap-free finite range 200000000000<=n<N with every survivor eliminated under declared imported premises, or a proved new necessary condition.
shared_scope_rules: No automatic revisit, refill, extra problem, paid-API fallback, model/config change, scheduler, commit, push, or external contact.
A special case, finite search range, or improved bound is partial progress, not resolution of a broader book question.
Sampling is not independent exhaustive verification. Numerical negativity is not a theorem without its analytic bridge. Solver UNKNOWN is not UNSAT.
Openness and novelty are dated search verdicts. Preprints and openai/math are claims until independently established.
shared_review_overrides: This manifest and parent restrictions override stronger promises, confidence labels, and schedules in the screening catalogs.
The 14,400-second attack is part of each 21,600-second visit, not an extra allowance. Early termination and inconclusive outcomes are valid; no refill is implied.
Reserve new best, improved, or novel wording for the visit literature and novelty assessments; reproduction and restricted results keep their exact scope.

The replay sandbox forbids executing binaries created inside the attack directory. Every claims.json verify/check/control command must run with python3 or preinstalled system tools; preserve compiled-production logs as evidence instead.
